items.evidence: From no engine running, 'node tools/kit.js build' (in work/) ran in 26 s, exit 0, and printed a JSON array for gear/heart/star/coin with name, triangles (320/980/36/764), closed (true x4) and bounds x/y/z min-max. The engine started with no window and was stopped again afterwards.

I deleted frames/*.png and ran 'node tools/kit.js frames' (exit 0). It rewrote frames/gear,heart,star,coin.png, each reported as 512x512. I opened all four: each prop is fully in view and centred, seen from the front.

frames/gear.png shows 12 identical straight-flanked teeth, evenly spaced, and a round centre hole with the dark background visible through it. My own oblique sight_frame (eye 0.25,0.25,0.4) shows the hole bore and background through it. Recipe: gear outline teeth 12, hole cylinder r 0.03 cut through.
Build bounds for gear: x -0.149998..0.149998 (0.3 wide), y 0.0000018..0.299998 (0.3 tall, stands on y=0), z -0.025..0.025 (0.05 thick). All well within 5%.

frames/heart.png reads clearly as a heart: two round lobes on top with a notch, and a point at the bottom. The edges show a bevel band. My oblique frame (eye 0.3,0.3,0.3) shows rounded, beveled edges around the side (recipe bevel 0.012, 3 segments). Bounds 0.3 wide, 0.05 thick.
frames/star.png shows a five-pointed star, upright, with sharp, evenly spaced points. Build bounds: x -0.14998..0.14998 (0.3 across), z -0.025..0.025 (0.05 thick), y from ~0.

Coin bounds: x -0.1..0.1 (0.2 across), y 0..0.2, z -0.01..0.01 (0.02 thick). The front frame shows a disc with a faint inner ring. My two oblique sight_frames, of the front face (eye 0.2,0.16,0.12) and the back face (eye -0.2,0.16,-0.12), both show a raised rim wall around a recessed face. The recipe cuts a 0.003-deep r 0.085 recess in each face, so the middle is 0.014 thick against a 0.02 rim, and the rim is 0.015 wide.

The headless build printed closed: true for all four (closedness computed by tools/kit.js from the engine's glTF export: weld plus each directed edge used once each way). All four recipes take materials from the one assets/style.json (steel/gold/ruby satin presets; the model_build output names that style file). The frames show a consistent look: flat chunky tokens with the same lighting and finish.

README gives 'node tools/kit.js build' and 'node tools/kit.js frames', to be run from work/ with no engine. I ran both exactly so, from a state with no engine serving. Both worked and both left no engine running.

defects: The 'closed' flag is the kit's own edge test on the exported glTF, not the engine's report. The README admits it was never tried on a known-open mesh, and I did not test it against one either.
The heart's outline is hand-made (two circular lobes on a right-angled point) rather than the library heart. It reads fine but is a little stiff, as the README says. It is 0.274 tall for 0.3 wide.
The coin's front frame shows the rim only faintly (a thin ring). The raised rim is clear only from an angle, and the README's frames give no angled view.
The frames command leaves engine capture folders under work/captures each time it runs.
